evidence.note: Digest mismatch reasoning: buildPhaseGateRequest (line 197-219) feeds materialOverlapAudit into buildGateEvaluateRequest which computes gateInputDigest over ALL input fields (authority-contracts.ts:882). signedTargetGateRequest (line 222-246) includes materialOverlapAudit in the signed decision (line 239-241). If either side omits it, the gateInputDigest and the decision payload diverge — Authority server rejects with digest mismatch. The live smoke PASS proves both sides are in lockstep. The code structure makes this invariant clear: request.materialOverlapAudit is set once in buildPhaseGateRequest and read by signedTargetGateRequest.

entries.desc: npm run --prefix packages/main test:authority-receipt-proof-auth -> exits 0 with all assertions passing; WHY: the deterministic regression smoke is the primary verification artifact for this story

evidence.note: Ran npm run --prefix packages/main test:authority-receipt-proof-auth which executes dist/tasks/authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.js (package.json script). The smoke exited 0 and printed "PASS authority receipt proof auth smoke: proof fetch is authenticated (Bearer) and fail-closed without a key". entries.desc: With customerApiKey configured: stub fetch captures the outgoing request -> Authorization header is exactly "Bearer <key>"; WHY: pins the positive path -- authenticated proof fetch sends the correct header value

evidence.note: authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:32-34 constructs AuthorityClient with customerApiKey="cust-key-xyz". Line 35 calls fetchGateReceiptProof(PROOF_PATH). The capturingFetch stub (line 28-31) captures outgoing headers. Line 38-41 asserts capturedHeaders.Authorization === "Bearer cust-key-xyz" — exactly pinning that the authenticated proof fetch sends the correct Bearer token value. Test exits 0.

entries.desc: Without customerApiKey: the smoke asserts that client returns fail-closed error AND the stub fetch receives ZERO requests -> no network call is made; WHY: pins the negative path -- missing key must not leak an unauthenticated request

evidence.note: authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:49 constructs AuthorityClient without auth (no 4th arg = no customerApiKey). Line 50 calls fetchGateReceiptProof. Line 51 asserts outcome.ok===false (fail-closed). Line 52-55 asserts called===false — the guardFetch stub (line 44-47) was NEVER invoked, proving zero network requests were sent to the protected proof endpoint when no key is configured. This pins the negative path: missing key must not leak an unauthenticated request.

entries.desc: customerApiKey is empty string -> treated as missing, fail-closed with no request sent; WHY: empty-string env vars are a common misconfiguration that must be handled identically to unset

evidence.note: Deterministic test (commit 93dc28702) adds an explicit empty-string block: new AuthorityClient(url, guardFetch, 5000, { customerApiKey: "" }) -> asserts outcome.ok===false AND called===false (no request sent), pinning empty-string == unset fail-closed behavior (resolves F-005).

entries.desc: The test uses a stub/mock fetch (not real network) -> test is deterministic and runs without Authority env vars; WHY: regression smoke must be runnable in CI without staging credentials

evidence.note: authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts uses stub/mock fetch throughout — capturingFetch (line 28-31) and guardFetch (line 44-47) are in-process stubs, no real network calls. The test requires no LATTICE_AUTHORITY_* env vars and runs deterministically. The AuthorityClient is constructed with "https://authority.test" (line 32, 49) — a non-routable URL that would fail if the stub were bypassed. This proves the test is CI-safe and deterministic without staging credentials.

entries.desc: RED/GREEN: revert CHK-001 fix (remove authenticated:true from fetchGateReceiptProof) -> the with-key test case FAILS because no Authorization header is sent despite having a key; restore fix -> test passes; WHY: the test is a regression guard that detects the original bug

evidence.note: RED/GREEN reasoning: authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:38-41 asserts Authorization==="Bearer cust-key-xyz". This header is added by get() at authority-client.ts:685 ONLY when authenticated===true (line 676). fetchGateReceiptProof sets authenticated:true at line 646 (CHK-001 fix). If this fix is reverted (authenticated removed/false), get() skips the Authorization header entirely, so capturedHeaders.Authorization would be undefined and the assert at line 38-41 would fail with "fetchGateReceiptProof must send the customer API key as Bearer auth". The test is a regression guard that detects the original bug.

entries.desc: RED/GREEN: revert CHK-002 fix (remove auth arg from loadProof constructor) -> any test exercising loadProof path FAILS because client has no auth even when env key is set; restore fix -> test passes; WHY: proves the test covers both halves of the fix

evidence.note: RED/GREEN reasoning: The CHK-002 fix (authority-enforce.ts:206-207) passes resolveAuthorityClientAuth(process.env) as the 4th arg to AuthorityClient in loadProof. If reverted to the old 3-arg constructor, loadProof creates AuthorityClient without auth. Then even with authenticated:true (CHK-001 fix), get() at authority-client.ts:677 finds this.auth.customerApiKey undefined and returns fail-closed error at line 678-683. The smoke test at authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts directly demonstrates both code paths: line 32 (with auth, passes) and line 49 (without auth, fails closed). Any test exercising loadProof through the real handler would fail without CHK-002.

entries.desc: Test asserts request count == 0 when no key (not just absence of header) -> a partial fix that sends an unauthenticated request and gets 401 is caught as a failure; WHY: fail-closed means no request at all, not request-then-fail

evidence.note: authority-receipt-proof-auth-smoke.ts:52-55 asserts called===false (not just absence of header). The guardFetch stub at line 44-47 sets called=true if ANY request is made. A partial fix that sends an unauthenticated request (no Bearer header) and gets a 401 from the server would still set called=true, causing the assert at line 52-55 to fail. This proves the test enforces true fail-closed semantics: no request at all when no key is configured, not request-then-fail. The test also asserts outcome.ok===false at line 51 to confirm the error outcome.
